Conjecture: Coarse-Equivalence Invariance of Protocol-Pullback Multiplicity Across Bit-Permuted Gadgets
Statement: Let G_1 = (X, Y, g, d) be a MetricGadget on small alphabet (|X|,|Y| ≤ 4) and let G_2 be obtained from G_1 by a bi-Lipschitz bijection φ: X×Y → X×Y with distortion ≤ 2 (a coarse equivalence: φ permutes inputs while distorting d by at most a factor 2). Fix any boolean f: {0,1}^n → {0,1} with n ≤ 4. Then for every deterministic protocol Π_1 computing f∘G_1^n, there exists a deterministic protocol Π_2 computing f∘G_2^n with cost cost(Π_2) ≤ cost(Π_1) + O(n), and the multiplicities of their CoarsePullback covers at scale R = diam(G) satisfy m_{Π_2} ≤ 2 · m_{Π_1} + 1. Equivalently, CLC(f,G_1) and CLC(f,G_2) agree up to a constant factor independent of f, instantiating Axiom A1 (Coarse-Lift Functoriality) at the level of the multiplicity invariant that A2 connects to communication complexity.
Strategy: 1. Implement a MetricGadget on |X|=|Y|=2 (so X×Y has 4 points) with the standard inner-product gadget g(x,y)=x·y mod 2 and Hamming distance d. 2. Enumerate all bi-Lipschitz bijections φ on X×Y of distortion ≤ 2 (there are at most 24 permutations; filter by distortion ≤ 2). 3. For n ∈ {2,3,4} and f ranging over a sample of 16 boolean functions on n bits, brute-force enumerate all deterministic communication protocols of small cost (via decision-tree search up to depth 2n+2) computing f∘G_1^n, recording each Π's transcript partition. 4. For each protocol Π_1, compute m_{Π_1} as the minimum cover multiplicity at scale R = diam(G) = 2 obtained by grouping the (X×Y)^n inputs by transcript and taking d_⊕-balls. 5. Construct Π_2 by pre-composing Π_1 with φ coordinatewise (cost overhead bounded by O(n) communication of φ-images), and recompute m_{Π_2}. 6. Verify m_{Π_2} ≤ 2·m_{Π_1} + 1 across all (f, Π_1, φ) triples. 7. Report the empirical maximum ratio m_{Π_2}/m_{Π_1}; the conjecture predicts this stays ≤ 2 + o(1). All steps fit in <90s since |(X×Y)^n| ≤ 256 and the protocol/permutation space is small.

Write the pre-registration JSON now.
